prompt: A full-body character illustration for a fantasy lookbook: one man, Ser Darrow, on a solid {screen} background. If the design's At his side line names a companion, they are in the picture with him; otherwise he is alone.
Reference images, attached in this order:
Design (draw exactly this; whatever the references show that is not listed here is replaced):

He is thirty-two, tall, with grey-green eyes in a lean, weathered face and a nose broken once and set a little crooked, with a faint scar across the bridge. Take his face from Image 1 and do not change his facial features, eye colour, skin tone or the shape of his nose, even when his beard, hair or expression changes. His body is the one the Build line describes, his face wears the Expression line, and the Pose line alone says how he stands, sits or moves.

Painterly fantasy concept art in the hand-painted style of Image 2: visible, elegant brushwork; believable weathered medieval wool, linen, leather and steel with detailed stitching; soft, warm, natural light; grounded historical fantasy. Not a photograph, not a 3D render, not a cartoon.

Vertical 2:3 portrait (1024 x 1536) at the same scale and framing as Image 2: his whole figure, and his companion's if there is one, from the top of his head to his feet, with a comfortable margin on every side. Background: one solid, flat {screen} filling the whole frame behind him, edge to edge: no gradient, no texture, no glow, no vignette, nothing painted onto it. No backdrop, no floor, no ground shadow, no frame, no text, no watermark; the only scenery is what the Pose line itself names (a stool, a post, a few steps). Keep that colour off him: nothing he wears or holds is that colour, and it casts no light or reflection on him or anyone with him.
- No other people and no animals beyond the companion the At his side line names.
- He wears and holds only what the design names; where a line says none, leave that thing off him entirely.
- Check every line of the design before finishing.
